title: CSS Hide Elements
text:
CSS
Hide
Elements



CSS display: none;

When using
display: none;
the element is completely hidden from the document flow
and does not take
up any space.

It is commonly used with JavaScript to hide
or show elements without deleting and recreating them.

Click to show hidden panel

This panel contains a <div> element, which is hidden by default, with display: none.

We use JavaScript to show it (change it to display: block).

Hiding an element can be done by setting the
display
property to

none
.
The element will be hidden, and the page will be displayed as if the element is not
there:

You can also use
visibility:hidden;
to hide an element.

However, with this property, the element will be hidden, but it will still take up the same space
as if it was visible:

CSS Display/Visibility Properties

Property

Description

display

Specifies how an element should be displayed

visibility

Specifies whether or not an element should be visible
